chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Musa ibn 'Umarah from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Aban from Muhammad ibn Mudarib who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say about a man who curses his wife before he has had intercourse with her?' He said: 'He is not a mutla' (one who performs li'an) until he has had intercourse with her; he is flogged and she is his wife, and he is a qadhf (one who gives false testimony of zina).'.

key_terms.قَاذِفاً: one who gives false testimony of zina
key_terms.لَعَنَ: cursed (specifically in the context of li'an)
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: he enters with her (consummation of marriage)
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ حَدّاً: he is flogged (receives the hadd penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an if it occurs before marital consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a critical juristic distinction: pre-consummation cursing does not trigger the full 'li'an' procedure for divorce, but rather results in the husband being flogged for 'qadhf' (false accusation) while the marital bond remains intact. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical consummation of marriage as a prerequisite for the specific legal consequences of li'an, differentiating it from the general penalty for false testimony.
